content.title: About
content.content: Solid Oaxaca cheese is a traditional Mexican semi‑hard cheese made from cow's milk. It has a mild, slightly nutty flavor and an elastic texture that makes it easy to slice and grate. The cheese is commonly used in tacos, enchiladas, casseroles, and other classic dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The cheese is named after the Mexican state of Oaxaca, where it originated.
The solid version is aged longer than the soft variety, giving it a firmer structure.
It stretches into strings similar to mozzarella, making it popular for melted dishes.
In Mexico it is often served as “cheese strands” pulled on a hot skillet.
Oaxaca cheese is widely exported to the US and Canada for use in Mexican cuisine.

items.title: Rich in calcium
items.content: Provides a high amount of calcium, essential for bone and teeth health.

items.title: Good source of protein
items.content: Supplies high‑quality animal protein needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains B12 and B2, supporting energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Phosphorus and zinc
items.content: These minerals aid immune function and metabolic processes.

items.title: Probiotic properties
items.content: Fermentation promotes beneficial bacteria that support gut health.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Lactose content may cause discomfort for those who are lactose intolerant.

items.title: High in saturated fat
items.content: The cheese contains saturated fats, so it should be consumed in moderation.

items.title: Milk allergy
items.content: People allergic to dairy may experience reactions.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Often salty; individuals with hypertension should watch portion size.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Solid Oaxaca cheese can be cubed, grated, or pulled into strands. It works well as a taco filling, in casseroles, salads, or as a snack. Pairs nicely with tomatoes, avocado, fresh herbs, and spicy sauces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cheese in the refrigerator wrapped in parchment paper or plastic wrap, then place in an airtight container. At 2‑4 °C it stays fresh for 4‑6 weeks. Freezing is possible but may alter texture.
